summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of pseudotumor cerebri and a VP shunt presented with persistent right lower quadrant abdominal pain. Evaluation included normal labs, a KUB showing unchanged shunt position, and a CT abdomen confirming no fluid collection, mass, or obstruction. Surgical and neurosurgical teams found no indication for intervention. Pain was managed with an increased dose of amitriptyline and a short course of hydrocodone. Her diabetes was managed with temporary insulin, later transitioning back to oral glyburide. Iron and vitamin D deficiencies were addressed with supplementation. She was discharged home with follow-up plans for pain management, depression, and monitoring of elevated alkaline phosphatase.
